scope: Eighteenth expansion batch: 12 exercises. Three shared exclusive-limit items cover a single opportunity, being alone and a two-person conversation; three approximate-count items supply reciprocal contrast. Three Vta-kiri items practice a completed event without follow-up up to a reference point, contrasted with three Vru-tabi-ni recurring follow-ups using the same verbs. This is not independent discrimination among valid limit expressions, nor complete coverage of kiri, kagiri or tabi.

sources.section: Actual HTML heading きり［副助］, not the homonymous plant or Portuguese-derived キリ entries: sense 1a for exclusive limitation, sense 1b for continuing state, sense 2 for no further action after a last event, often with a negative predicate, and sense 3 for only/except with negative expressions. The introductory note recognizes kkiri and giri. Simplified extraction returned only the paulownia encyclopedia entry; the dictionary body was inspected separately.

sources.publisher: Shogakukan, Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten via Kotobank
sources.section: Heading きり【切・限】: particle section [2], especially sense 1 for dake/kagiri limitation; suffix section [3]6b for tak-kiri and remaining in a state. This dictionary's classification is kept distinct from Daijisen's particle treatment. Daijisen's separate kanji-heading entry on this page covers noun and counter uses, not the modern particle entry on the kana-heading page.

Exact 切り entry read kiri, not 霧, 桐, 錐 or other homophones: particle senses only/just, since/after and continuing state; usually written in kana. Recognizes 切り/限り/切/限. Dictionary recognition does not establish equal frequency or readability of these spellings in the authored sentences.

Separately inspected the 限り entry read kagiri and its suffix/adverbial sense '... only', exemplified in the gloss by one-time-only and today-only. The search also returns the different kiri entry; these readings are not conflated.
Exact 出掛ける entry: both 出かける and 出掛ける have the reading dekakeru and the unrestricted ichidan-verb go-out/leave senses. Both written stems and full kana are accepted in the outing exercises.

Main lesson on formal noun/verb-attached limitation with nomi, compared with dake; the explicit caution excludes automatic substitution for dake's degree/extent uses. Formality alone does not disqualify nomi in the selected neutral limit tasks.

Main lesson: an event occurring on every occasion, with direct verb attachment and noun + no; the activity/event sense rather than a bare travel meaning. Used for the dictionary-form verb patterns already documented in the time batch.

reusedSourceRecords.scope: Inspected record of the actual JMdict particle entries for hodo, kurai/gurai, bakari and dake, and context-dependent quantity uses. The same eight uncontracted approximate-answer spellings are retained. The record's warning against treating bakari as incapable of limitation still applies; its suitability must be judged in the whole sentence.
Existing recurring-occasion coverage and verb/noun attachment for tabi-ni; the Bunpro main lesson was additionally fetched for this batch.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are original. Sources support constructions, not automatic naturalness of each new example or completeness of its answer list; retain independent linguistic review.

The first six tasks visibly name eight uncontracted particle forms/families. Their learning goal is exclusive limitation versus estimation, not choosing kiri over a suitable equivalent. The three limit answers accept dake and nomi as well as kiri; the opportunity item also accepts kagiri. Nomi's more formal style is explained, not penalized. Colloquial kkiri is explained in feedback and the article but is outside this particular uncontracted-form task.

The written form kagiri/kiri share does not make their kana readings interchangeable in every collocation. The person-limit items accept 限り as a kiri spelling without claiming 一人かぎり or 二人かぎり is the ordinary equivalent of being alone or just the two of us. Kana is recommended; dictionary spellings are accepted recognition, not a frequency claim.

The three estimates accept hodo, kurai/gurai and bakari together, and use a different representative model in each example. Zen-go and further approximation paraphrases remain outside the visible named families. Kiri is a real limit alternative, not a deliberately malformed distractor; the visible meaning task determines why it is unsuitable.

The latter six tasks explicitly request Vta + kiri or Vru + tabi-ni without extra particles. This practices whole-pattern attachment together with last-event versus recurring-event meaning. Kana and kanji spellings, including 出かけ/出掛け, and colloquial kkiri are accepted. The same three verbs appear on both sides, including the irregular suru past in denwa-shita.

The article inventory was screened: mama and te-irai/te-kara can also describe a since-then or unchanged-state situation, and goto-ni, toki and other formulations can describe occasions. These are not globally invalid; they are outside the visible two-pattern task. A bare only gloss is not adequate for every ta-kiri use.

The book loan lacks a different follow-up action, returning, rather than another borrowing. The morning departure is viewed from noon with a later return planned. The call gap ends with renewed contact today and is explicitly viewed through yesterday. None licenses a permanent-consequence, first-ever-action or never-again rule.

Supplementary https://bunpro.jp/grammar_points/きり was inspected for discovery. Its broad claims about the first and last time, almost always happening only once and permanent consequences are not adopted. Daijisen's exact limitation/no-further-action senses and the stated reference time control the explanations.

All 233 previous exercises remain unchanged against the committed baseline plus the recorded uncommitted you set. The shared article gains one scoped subsection, a particle-neighbor heading update and references; no existing teaching passage is removed. Each new exercise keeps one SRS identity regardless of accepted spelling or presentation.
